title: Air-gapped usage sync: watermark protocol and tamper-evident manifests
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Problem: Private/VPC and air-gapped customers often cannot ship realtime usage events to our hosted metering pipeline. We must guarantee correct accounting, avoid double-billing or missed usage, and preserve quota enforcement semantics when syncs are delayed by hours/days. Current exported bundles are opaque and rely on last-write heuristics, which complicates reconciliation and forces manual investigations for customers.

Goal: Design and implement a robust watermark-based incremental export protocol for on-prem agents that produces tamper-evident manifests, supports idempotent replay into the hosted billing pipeline, and enables deterministic reconciliation/backfill with strong security properties (signed manifests, non-replayable bundle ids). The system should: (1) allow the hosted billing ledger to unambiguously apply or skip bundles, (2) detect gaps and overlaps, (3) provide SLOs for eventual reconciliation, and (4) be operable by Customer Success during incidents.
design_decisions: 1) Use a monotonically-increasing per-agent export watermark (wall-clock + sequence) persisted in local ledger; exports include start_watermark and end_watermark. 2) Each export bundle gets a cryptographic manifest signed by customer KMS or agent key; hosted ingestion verifies signatures and manifest hash. 3) Bundles are chunked into size-limited archives (<= 500MB) with per-chunk checksums and a top-level manifest. 4) Host ingestion performs dedup by (agent_id, end_watermark, manifest_hash). 5) Backfills are labeled explicitly and cannot be merged with incremental exports; they are applied via a defined backfill path that runs reconciliation checks before committing charges. 6) Local agent enforces a local soft quota and per-customer rate-limiter with grace tokens and adjustment metadata so offline operation doesn't silently overconsume. 7) Failure modes (partial upload, corrupted bundle) are handled by deterministic retry windows and quarantined manifests for manual review.
implementation_notes: - Local ledger schema: usage_rows table (timestamp, model_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, operation_id, sequence), export_cursor table (last_watermark, last_sequence, pending_bundle_id). - Export packaging: tar.gz archive containing usage.csv (newline delimited per operation), manifest.json, chunk_checksums.txt, signature.sig. - Manifest fields: agent_id, export_id (UUID v1), start_watermark (ISO8601+seq), end_watermark, row_count, token_totals, archive_size_bytes, chunk_count, parent_bundle_ids (for splits), signing_key_id. - Signing: agent supports customer-provided key (KMS/HSM) or generated ephemeral key; host ingestion accepts signatures signed by registered keys. - Ingestion: idempotency key = sha256(agent_id + end_watermark + manifest_hash). If ingestion sees existing idempotency key, it skips and records "duplicate". - Quota adjustments: when a bundle arrives referencing a grace-period token allowance, the hosted quota reconciler either consumes grace tokens or marks overage for potential credit pending manual review. - Reconciliation: run streaming diff between ledger view and applied-hosted-charges for window [start_watermark,end_watermark]. If mismatch > threshold, create incident and attach raw bundle for audit. - Offline export retention: agents keep last 90 days of bundles; manifests older than 365 days are auto-pruned after manual export to cold storage. - Edge: handle clock skew by allowing +/- 5m tolerance in watermark ordering and by relying on per-operation sequence numbers for exact ordering.
testing_plan: - Unit: manifest generation/verification, signature verification, idempotency key logic, local ledger watermark advance. - Integration: end-to-end with an airgap emulator that simulates intermittent connectivity and partial uploads. Ingest emulator uses same dedup logic as the service. - Load testing: simulate a 5k-rps local workload producing hourly bundles; verify packaging time, CPU/memory, and ingest throughput. - Fuzzing: corrupt chunk checksums and ensure ingestion quarantines bundles without applying charges. - Reconciliation tests: inject controlled duplication and missing rows to validate alert thresholds and backfill path. - Security: key rotation tests and rejection of manifests signed by unknown keys. - Acceptance: run with two pilot customers (one VPC, one on-prem) for 4 weeks, verify end-to-end no-billing-drift for >99.995% of usage windows.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Host ingestion rejects or dedups duplicates deterministically (no manual dedup required). 2) Reconciliation job detects >99.9% of non-trivial mismatches within 1 hour of bundle arrival. 3) Pilot customers report no unexplained charge deltas after 4-week pilot. 4) API docs and Confluence runbook for CS/ops completed and reviewed. 5) Security review signed off for manifest signing and key management.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): ship agent v1 to internal QA and two pilot tenants; disable automatic quota enforcement differences (run in audit-only mode). Phase 2: enable automated ingestion with dedup/skip logic for pilot tenants; run reconciliation with human-in-the-loop approvals for any mismatches. Phase 3: roll to all private customers with opt-in; provide migration tool for older bundles to be re-wrapped into manifests. Phase 4: GA and deprecate legacy opaque bundles. Rollout includes a 2-week freeze window for support and a post-deployment retrospective. Rollback: if reconciliation mismatch rate >0.1% or any signed-manifest verification regression, pause ingestion and revert to audit-only processing.
monitoring_alerts: Dashboards: PrivateUsage/IngestRate, PrivateUsage/DedupRate, PrivateUsage/ReconciliationMismatch, PrivateUsage/BundleCorruption. Alerts: P1 if ReconciliationMismatch rate >0.05% over 1h, P0 if bundle signature verification failures >10 in 10m, P1 if ingest backlog >2 hours for more than 30m. Create SLOs for eventual reconciliation (90% within 10m, 99% within 1h, 99.9% within 24h).
